headlines.title: Utility Spending Plans Grow as Large New Power Customers Sign On
headlines.summary: American News Group News Commentary - Third-quarter results season brought larger multi-year spending plans and longer growth outlooks from several U.S. utilities as they plan for new large customers. Across their reports, companies described gigawatts of new load commitments signed, data center demand under contract, and tens of billions of dollars in planned investment in transmission, generation and distribution.

headlines.title: AEP or Public Service Enterprise: The One Dividend Stock I’d Hold for the Next 10 Years
headlines.summary: Key TakeawaysAmerican Electric Power raised its quarterly dividend 2. 1% in October and now forecasts dividend growth of roughly 2% a year over the next four to five years.

headlines.title: Can American Electric Power (AEP) Keep Growing Earnings at 22%?
headlines.summary: We just published a list of the Top 10 Stocks to Buy According to Billionaire George Soros, and American Electric Power Company, Inc. (NASDAQ:AEP) ranked 9th on this list. George Soros made his name betting against currencies and central banks, and that record is still the reference point for macro investing decades later.

headlines.title: American Electric Power Company (AEP) Seeks PJM Role, Is The Stock Fully Valued?
headlines.summary: American Electric Power Company (AEP) moved to intervene in a Federal Energy Regulatory Commission proceeding, arguing that its utilities and marketing arm could be directly affected by decisions shaping PJM Interconnection power markets. Recent price action for American Electric Power Company has cooled, with the share price down 3.1% over the past week and 1.8% over 30 days, even though the 90-day share price return of 3.3% and 1-year total shareholder return of 6.

headlines.title: How Many Shares of Duke Energy, Consolidated Edison or AEP Pay $1,000 a Month in Dividends?
headlines.summary: Key TakeawaysAt today’s prices, $1,000 a month in dividends takes 2,765 shares of Duke Energy, 3,093 shares of American Electric Power or 3,381 shares of Consolidated Edison. Duke Energy costs the least, about $358,800, which is about $44,700 less than Consolidated Edison, but it pays out the most of its earnings: 67% of fiscal 2025 normalized EPS.

description: American Electric Power Company, Inc., an electric public utility holding company, engages in the generation, transmission, and distribution of electricity for sale to retail and wholesale customers in the United States. It operates through Vertically Integrated Utilities, Transmission and Distribution Utilities, AEP Transmission Holdco, and Generation & Marketing segments. The company generates electricity using coal and lignite, nuclear, natural gas, renewable, hydro, solar, wind, and other energy sources; owns, operates, maintains, and invests in transmission infrastructure; and engages in the retail supply, and wholesale energy trading and marketing businesses. It operates approximately 252,000 circuit miles of distribution lines; 38,000 circuit miles of transmission lines; and 25,000 MWs of regulated owned generating capacity. American Electric Power Company, Inc. was incorporated in 1906 and is headquartered in Columbus, Ohio.
